messages:
elaine: Heads-up — after the kernel-selection change landed in runtime (9f4a3b -> 9f4a3c) we see a 7-12% host CPU increase on ingress for small chat requests. p95 tokenization+parse time jumped. filing here before a full postmortem.

kevin: ugh, saw the spike in the dashboard. is it strictly the tokenization stage or the HTTP/gRPC layer too?

elaine: traces point at two hotspots: our JSON parsing path and streaming chunk assembly in host-proxy. quick pprof excerpt:
```
  32.4%  tokenization_pool::tokenize
  18.1%  http2::stream::read_frame
  12.9%  request_parser::parse_json_body
   9.0%  writev_flush
   7.6%  kvcache::lookup
```

tessa: can you paste the sample request shape? small prompt, `max_tokens=64`, streaming enabled?

elaine: yes. typical: streaming=true, ~120B prompt, 60-80 tokens output. reproducer curl below:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.local/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DEV" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","stream":true,"input":"short prompt"}'
```

kevin: odd — that workload should benefit from batching. But host-side overhead for tiny requests dominates. suspecting extra syscalls from framing.

infra-bot: deploy 9f4a3c rolled to canary at 2026-03-17T14:22:10Z :rocket:

ryan: two quick experiments:
  1) try `use_proto_ingress=true` to skip JSON parse and see delta.
  2) disable `MSG_MORE` hint removal (we recently toggled it on windows of stream coalescing).

tessa: also check `http2_max_concurrent_streams` — if it's too low we serialize frames and add latency.

elaine: ran proto toggle on canary for 10k requests: host CPU dropped ~6% and p95 parse time down 20ms. so JSON parse is significant.

kevin: great signal. can we micro-opt JSON path? we have a char-by-char streaming parser that does many tiny allocations.

elaine: yeah that parser is ancient. one idea: fast-path for small payloads: pre-allocated stack buffer + `memchr`-driven parse for strings. also reuse tokenizer buffers across requests using freelist instead of new each time.

ryan: we also added an extra layer of `RequestEnvelope` copy in gateway when attaching trace headers; that's cheap but for tiny requests it's not.

tessa: proposal: revert 9f4a3c commit that introduced the extra copy and enable proto by default for internal traffic. short rollback might buy time.

kevin: before revert, try `writev` batching tweak: group body frames into single writev for streaming chunks. reduces syscall count for streaming clients.

elaine: perf test with writev batching + proto ingress enabled:
  - host CPU: -11%
  - p95 latency: -28ms
  - p99 unchanged

ryan: good. p99 unchanged suggests backend/gpu still dominant occasionally.

tessa: any KV-cache interaction? we saw a small increase in kvcache lookups at same time.

elaine: kvcache hits stable, but lookup overhead increased because parser holds a mutex longer while assembling keys. moving key assembly outside the lock reduced kv lookup CPU by 3%.

kevin: safe checklist for a hotfix PR:
  - [ ] enable proto ingress for internal traffic
  - [ ] implement writev streaming coalesce
  - [ ] move key assembly outside kv lock
  - [ ] add small-request fast-path for JSON (stack buffer)
  - [ ] add pprof sampling test in perf harness

elaine: starting a branch now, will open PR with benchmarks. linking canary perf graphs in the PR.

ryan: ping me on the PR, I can help with the proto rollout gating and metrics.

tessa: add a tiny unit test that simulates 50k small streaming requests to catch regressions.

elaine: will do. rough ETA: hotfix PR by EOD, canary toggle in 2 hours.

kevin: thanks team. after hotfix we should add an ingress microbenchmark to CI that runs on every kernel-selection change.

elaine: agree — adding perf gating to the `runtime-change` job.

infra-bot: perf job queued: runtime-change-small-requests-2001234567

elaine: final note — labeling this thread `investigation:host-ingress-small-reqs` for follow-up docs. :spiral_notepad:

kevin: nice work. follow-up doc in docs/perf when fixed.
